correctness.rationale: For n=3^a m, 3 does not divide m, the multiplicative numerator h(n)=sum_{d|n} d phi(d) has exact valuation K(m)=sum_{p^e||m,p=2 mod 3}v_3(2e+1), by lifting the exponent. Thus 3 divides the reduced denominator iff a>K(m). Summing a>K(m) gives the exact nonnegative Dirichlet series; p-local first-order cancellation establishes F(s)=zeta(s)^alpha(s)L(s,chi)^beta(s)G(s) with alpha(1)=2/3, beta(1)=1/3, and G analytic/nonzero at one. In a slit zero-free neighborhood the variable exponent changes the leading singularity only by O((s-1)log(1/|s-1|)); standard Perron/Hankel Selberg--Delange extraction gives the displayed leading term. All Euler factors are positive at one and 1+O(p^-2), so C3>0. Actual standalone package verification independently compared 1000 exact rational sums, enumerated 500000 local predicates and checked a truncated constant; those finite checks are supplementary, not the asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating arXiv paper establishes global integrality bounds for H=h/n but does not characterize n for which a fixed prime remains in the reduced denominator. The inspected OEIS complement classes similarly do not give the ternary asymptotic. The exact 3-adic criterion, variable exponent a(s)=(1+3^(-s))/2, and the explicit convergent Euler constant were not identified in targeted primary-literature and published-record statement-level searches. General Selberg--Delange is only a method; an unindexed or unpublished equivalent result remains a real residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed prior calculation of the same local denominator distribution cannot be excluded.
The general coefficient-extraction theorem is standard; only its new specialisation and explicit arithmetic Euler factors are claimed original.
Other databases beyond the inspected complementary denominator entries might contain a matching prime-specific formula.

value.rationale: The fixed-prime reduced-denominator event is a natural local obstruction distinct from complete integrality in the motivating source. Its count has a nontrivial fractional logarithmic exponent 1/3 and a positive explicitly computable Euler-product constant, explaining the density-zero phenomenon and exact first-order rate for all positive integers. This is an infinite asymptotic for a naturally determined local invariant, not a small computational refinement or a routine direct reformulation of the existing integral-value bound.
